authority: #K2-242 sec.5 item (1): the MANDATORY product-comparison deliverable (2nd article). Read the staged product renders (/tmp/opencode/sup241_renders/, fetched by the supervisor per #K2-241 sec.3.5(b)); produce copy-what / apply-how, NOT 'already read'.
reference_case: library A / same chip PEX88096 - two boards by DESIGN:OLDMONSTER: (i) PEX88096-AIC-GEN4-10SLIMSAS-EVM Ver1.0 (10x SlimSAS '2S1525', upstream x16 gold-finger edge); (ii) PEX88096 GPUBoard GEN4 5CEM EVM Ver1.0 (4x PCIe slot + 5CEM SlimSAS). Both are the SAME silicon as K2's switch.

assets_read.what: silkscreen-layer render of the 10-SlimSAS AIC: the trace fan-out from the central switch to all 10 connectors is directly visible
back side of the family board: radial bundle fan-out from the BGA to the board edge
back side of the 5CEM board: bundle fan-out with s-bends only in the last few mm
both family boards side by side (AIC + GPUBoard)
5CEM board front: switch under heatsink, connectors on the perimeter
drill/copper plot: connector pin fields + BGA ball field
PCIe topology + SBR/STRAP bifurcation tables (5x16 / 2x8 / 4x4 / 8x2 / 16x1; STN0..STN5) => topology, not layout
tool screenshots / bench photos - no layout information

observed_layout_facts: The switch package sits at the board centre; the fan-out is a set of BUNDLES of straight parallel traces running from the BGA to each connector.
Every connector owns its own bundle at a uniform pitch; bundles are separated by wide gaps. There is no shared single-file corridor and no cross-section slot scheduling anywhere on the board.
The only bends in a bundle are shallow s-bends inside the last few mm, where the bundle expands into the connector's pad field. The long run is straight.
Each connector leg carries its OWN layer change at the breakout radius (via clustered next to the ball field), not deferred to a distant shared row.
Bifurcation (5x16/10x8/20x4/40x2/80x1) in the product is a CHIP-CONFIGURATION (SBR/STRAP) property, not a routing shape.

copy_what_apply_how.observe: one bundle per connector, uniform pitch, straight long run, s-bend only at the pad field
copy_what_apply_how.apply: K2 tail = one channel per lane, straight from the belt to the lane's own pad field. Lane pitch is the bundle pitch, not a shared grid row.

copy_what_apply_how.observe: no shared single-file cross-section; bundles simply do not overlap
copy_what_apply_how.apply: the exit-slot rule is NON-OVERLAP (distinct cell per layer). The product shows no >=2-cell spacing rule between exits.

copy_what_apply_how.observe: the layer change happens at the breakout (a via beside the ball field), early and on the lane's own column
copy_what_apply_how.apply: declare the lane's entrance layer transition explicitly (K2's own SPEC already declares it: In5_entrance for OUT3_N/OUT5_N/OUT6_N, DIVE_via for the COMB-start lanes).

copy_what_apply_how.observe: the connector's entry column is the connector's own fan-out column
copy_what_apply_how.apply: for OUT0_P (east, B pad at ~col 131 / row 4): enter the pad field on the lane's own column. K2's 'gate row 36' is K2-internal and has no product counterpart; the product reaches the connector directly, not via a shared row then a 33-row traverse.

named_conclusion: The product gives exactly one rule for the stuck lanes' tail: per-lane straight channel + one layer change at the breakout + non-overlap. It gives NO support for an exit-slot >=2 spacing rule, and NO support for deferring the layer change away from the lane's own column. This is independent, product-side corroboration of the rule-provenance audit (R634).
